title: Telemetry-guided gradient traffic rebalance for concurrent LLM sessions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a gradual, telemetry-driven traffic redistribution mechanism for the hosted API gateway to support active-active routing across regions while preserving LLM session continuity (including streaming responses and KV cache semantics). The goal is to avoid abrupt cutovers that break long-lived streaming sessions or cause large tail-latency regressions, and to tie redistribution decisions to SLO and telemetry signals (error rate, p95/p99 latency, in-flight token counts, KV cache hit ratio, circuit status).
acceptance_criteria: Can perform a staged traffic rebalance between Region A and Region B using small, incremental weight shifts (0.5-5% steps) driven by telemetry without user-visible stream interruptions
Streaming sessions (server-sent events / HTTP chunked) maintain continuity for >99.9% of active streams during a rebalance
SLO guardrails: if p99 latency or error rate exceeds configured thresholds during a step, rebalance pauses and triggers automated rollback within 30s
Circuit breakers open/close decisions are integrated and prevent traffic from shifting to degraded replicas
End-to-end integration tests and load test harness validate behavior with realistic LLM workloads, and results are documented in the runbook
tasks: Design: define telemetry signals and thresholds (latency, errors, inflight tokens, kv-cache-hit, connection churn)
Infra: extend gateway weight-controller to accept telemetry-driven directives and support micro-step adjustments
Runtime: ensure KV cache lookups and session metadata can be forwarded or short-lived sticky-proxies created during weight movement
Fallback: implement pause-and-rollback logic tied to circuit breaker state and a manual abort hook
Observability: dashboard for rebalance progress, per-region streaming continuity metrics, and SLO breakglass alerts
E2E: load tests with mixed short/long LLM sessions and streaming to validate continuity and SLO behavior
Docs/runbook: step-by-step play for ops and postmortem checklist
